a phospholipid bilayer, which arrangement is correct?","options":{"a":"Heads face water on both sides; tails are tucked inside.","b":"Tails face water on both sides; heads are tucked inside.","c":"Heads and tails both face water on the outside.","d":"Heads and tails both face inward, away from water."}},{"position":2,"concept_id":"c_fatty_acid_saturation","prompt":"Double bonds in an unsaturated fatty acid tail mainly:","options":{"a":"Straighten the tail, allowing tight packing.","b":"Increase packing density and lower fluidity.","c":"Kink the tail, hinder close packing, and raise fluidity.","d":"Lock the tail into the glycocalyx."}},{"position":3,"concept_id":"c_fluidity_factors","prompt":"Which of these is named as a factor that affects membrane fluidity?","options":{"a":"Tail saturation","b":"Amount of outer-surface sugar","c":"Leaflet asymmetry","d":"Flippase activity"}},{"position":4,"concept_id":"c_cholesterol_buffer","prompt":"In a very fluid membrane, cholesterol:","options":{"a":"Increases movement further.","b":"Restrains movement.","c":"Stiffens the membrane in the cold.","d":"Makes lipids switch leaflets freely."}},{"position":5,"concept_id":"c_cholesterol_buffer","prompt":"In cold conditions, cholesterol's role is to:","options":{"a":"Add to stiffening.","b":"Make the membrane more fluid.","c":"Convert tails into unsaturated tails.","d":"Prevent excessive stiffening."}},{"position":6,"concept_id":"c_fluid_mosaic_model","prompt":"The fluid mosaic model describes membrane components that can:","options":{"a":"Stay fixed in place.","b":"Switch leaflets without enzymes.","c":"Move sideways.","d":"Only be phospholipids."}},{"position":7,"concept_id":"c_membrane_asymmetry","prompt":"Lipids rarely switch between leaflets without:","options":{"a":"Cholesterol.","b":"Flippases, floppases, or composition.","b":"Are identical.","c":"Are made of protein only.","d":"Always switch positions."}},{"position":9,"concept_id":"c_glycocalyx_recognition","prompt":"Outer-surface sugars forming the glycocalyx help cells:","options":{"a":"Become more fluid.","b":"Pack their tails tightly.","c":"Form the inner leaflet.","d":"Distinguish self from non-self."}},{"position":10,"concept_id":"c_amphipathic_phospholipids","prompt":"Amphipathic describes a molecule that has:","options":{"a":"Both water-loving and water-avoiding parts.","b":"Only water-loving parts.","c":"Only water-avoiding parts.","d":"Sugar groups on its surface."}}]},"answer_key":[{"position":1,"correct_option":"a","rationale":"Water-loving heads face water on both sides of the bilayer, while water-avoiding tails are tucked inside."},{"position":2,"correct_option":"c","rationale":"Double bonds kink unsaturated tails, which makes close packing harder and increases membrane fluidity."},{"position":3,"correct_option":"a","rationale":"The explanation lists tail saturation, chain length, temperature, and cholesterol as factors affecting fluidity; the other options are not listed."},{"position":4,"concept_id":"c_cholesterol_buffer","correct_option":"b","rationale":"Cholesterol restrains movement when the membrane is very fluid, buffering fluidity in that condition."},{"position":5,"correct_option":"d","rationale":"In the cold, cholesterol prevents excessive stiffening, which is the buffering role described in the explanation."},{"position":6,"correct_option":"c","rationale":"The fluid mosaic model describes lipids, cholesterol, and proteins whose components can move sideways."},{"position":7,"correct_option":"b","rationale":"Lipids rarely switch leaflets without enzymes such as flippases, floppases, and scramblases."},{"position":8,"correct_option":"a","rationale":"The explanation says the two membrane leaflets differ in composition."},{"position":9,"correct_option":"d","rationale":"Glycocalyx sugars help cells recognize one another, including distinguishing self from non-self."},{"position":10,"correct_option":"a","rationale":"Amphipathic means a molecule has both water-loving and water-avoiding parts, as phospholipids do."}]}

tails"}},{"position":3,"concept_id":"c_fatty_acid_saturation","prompt":"Compared with a membrane made mostly of saturated tails, a membrane made mostly of unsaturated tails is likely to
